title: Bootcamp SnackShots: micro-bootcamp learning modules inside Console
creator: Hannah Kim
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, low-friction in-product learning layer called 'Bootcamp SnackShots' for the Redwood Console. SnackShots are 20-60 second interactive micro-lessons (inline tooltips, ephemeral micro-modals, and right-rail quickstarts) that teach common tasks: creating an API route, provisioning dedicated capacity, reading token cost breakdowns, and using rollout canaries. The goal is to increase first-week activation and reduce basic console support queries while keeping the UI uncluttered.

Goals & success metrics:
- Increase new-project 'first successful request' by 12% within 30 days.
- Reduce Console onboarding support tickets tagged 'how-to' by 30%.
- >70% completion rate for the first SnackShot sequence in early pilot.

User flows explored:
1) Contextual inline SnackShot: subtle highlight around the element (e.g., 'Create Route' button) with 2-step tooltip: explain action + short CTA that runs a guided action (prefilled form).
2) Right-rail Learning Dock: persistent, collapsible panel showing progress through SnackShot modules, templated starter kits, and a checklist to claim a 'Bootcamp complete' badge.
3) Modal micro-bootcamp: optional sequential micro-modals for new admins; auto-dismiss after first-run or available in Help menu.

Design principles & constraints:
- Non-intrusive: default is inline hint; modals are opt-in or permissioned by user setting.
- Lightweight assets: animation budget under 50ms frame work for perceived performance.
- Accessibility: full keyboard and screen-reader support; focus traps avoided for inline experiences.
- Telemetry-first: each SnackShot step emits an event for activation and completion (for PM and growth analysis).

Prototype & research links (see design_files): interactive Figma prototype with flows and annotated clickable states. Usability tests (n=12 remote sessions) run 2025-11-03 to 2025-11-06 with a mix of existing Redwood trial users and internal new-hire participants. Key findings: participants prefer inline hints over modals, templates were the most used artifact, and progress feedback improves confidence.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Inline vs persistent dock: Inline has lower disruption but can be missed; Dock helps rediscovery but costs right-rail real estate. Decision: default inline + optional dock toggle in Settings (saved per-org).
- Localization: translation pipeline required; MVP shipped only English with plan for i18n in next cycle.

Implementation notes for ENG:
- Add lightweight boolean flags to feature-flag service: snackshots.enabled and snackshots.dock_enabled.
- Telemetry events: snackshot.view, snackshot.start, snackshot.complete, snackshot.dismiss.
- Provide a JSON-driven content pack so SnackShot copy and steps are editable by PM without deploy.

Acceptance criteria (also listed below): user can opt-out; SnackShot sequence for 'Create Route' runs end-to-end in staging; telemetry fires for every step; templates button prepopulates and creates a sample project without errors.

Risks & mitigations:
- Overloading UI: keep SnackShots to essential first-run tasks and rotate content quarterly.
- Analytics noise: dedupe telemetry by session id and sample events if needed.
- Performance regressions: animations disabled on low-power devices; lazy-load dock assets.

Stakeholder approvals: PM (Jordan Lee) thumbs-up 2025-11-10; Eng lead (Luis Moreno) provided feasibility notes and recommended telemetry approach. Design critique requested from DES lead (Maya Singh) scheduled 2025-11-13.
acceptance_criteria: SnackShot inline hint for 'Create Route' appears for first-time project creators and can be dismissed for the session or always
Right-rail Learning Dock toggle appears in Settings and persists per-org
All SnackShot steps emit telemetry events (view, start, complete, dismiss)
Template button from SnackShot prepopulates form and creates sample project in staging without errors
Accessibility: screen reader reads hint content and keyboard navigation reaches all controls

decisions: Default experience: inline SnackShots, optional right-rail dock enabled by setting
Modal micro-bootcamp will be opt-in and not shown on first-run by default
Telemetry events and feature flags required before rollout
MVP will ship English-only; i18n planned in next milestone
